_what_this_is: THE AUTHORITATIVE, MACHINE-CHECKED RECORD OF HOW master IS PROTECTED. tools/validate-branch-protection.py reads this file, reads the LIVE state from GitHub, and FAILS the governance gate if they disagree. Documentation about protection that nothing verifies is how the previous gap survived: the rule text said four gates were required while GitHub required one, and no check could tell.
_mechanism: Repository RULESET, not classic branch protection. Classic protection was DELETED on 2026-09-10 because it could not express what was needed: its `enforce_admins: false` let the sole administrator bypass every requirement, and it offers no way to state 'nobody may bypass'. A ruleset with an EMPTY bypass_actors list applies to everyone including the repository owner, pins each required check to the GitHub Actions app so a renamed or third-party context cannot satisfy it, and records its own change history.
_reading_trap: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/master/protection now returns 'Branch not protected'. That endpoint reports CLASSIC protection only and knows nothing about rulesets. The authoritative reads are GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/master (effective rules) and GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets (enforcement and bypass actors). Both are readable without a token on this public repository, which is why CI can verify them on every run.

required_status_checks._integration_note: 15368 is the GitHub Actions app. Pinning it means a check of the same NAME reported by any other app or by a user token cannot satisfy the requirement.
required_status_checks._contexts_note: D42 (T0196), 2026-09-26: the single required context is the Product Owner merge authorization. It passes only while the pull request carries the label 'po-merge-approved' on the exact head being judged, and a later push removes the label (tools/po_merge_authorization.py). The four comprehensive gates -- governance, phase3-full-software-gate, phase4-financial-core-gate, phase5-post-stay-transfer-gate -- were required from 2026-09-10 until D42; they are now FULL CHECK THE WHOLE CODE only and are listed under full_check_gates.

pull_request._merge_method_note: Merge commits ONLY. Squash and rebase rewrite the tree, which would break the delivery-path property the CI evidence-reuse design depends on (the merge commit's tree being identical to the validated pull-request head) and would also destroy the one-to-one link between what was validated and what landed.
pull_request._approval_note: ZERO, and this is a measured constraint rather than a preference. The repository has exactly ONE collaborator (aibrahiiim1), who authors every delivery, and GitHub refuses self-approval - verified live, the API answers 'Review Can not approve your own pull request'. A non-zero requirement is therefore satisfiable only by granting an administrator bypass, which is precisely the silent-bypass hole this model exists to close. The choice made is universal enforcement of everything that CAN be enforced over a nominal requirement that only a bypass makes workable. Raising this to 1 requires a second reviewing account and is recorded as an open Product-Owner decision.

workflow_job_bindings._why: A required status context is a JOB NAME. Rename a job and the context never reports: the pull request can never go green, which is fail-closed but baffling, and the tempting 'fix' is to weaken the ruleset. This binding is asserted from the tree on every run so a rename is caught as an explicit error at pull-request time.

residual_risks.administrator_can_edit_the_rules: An administrator cannot bypass these rules at merge time - proven by live test - but can still edit or delete the ruleset itself. No plan-level control exists on a user-owned repository to prevent that; org-level rulesets with enterprise controls would be required. The mitigations in place are that ruleset changes are recorded in the ruleset's own history, and that tools/validate-branch-protection.py fails the governance gate the moment the live configuration stops matching this file - so any WEAKENING that leaves the rules in place is caught immediately. Outright deletion of the ruleset cannot be detected by a check that the ruleset is what makes required.
residual_risks.deletion_rule_not_isolated_in_test: The deletion rule is active, but the live attempt to delete master was refused by GitHub's inherent refusal to delete a repository's default branch, so the test could not isolate the rule's own contribution. Recorded as observed rather than claimed.
residual_risks.approval_actor_not_distinguishable: The Product Owner and the delivery agent act through the same GitHub account, so the merge-authorization check cannot tell WHO applied 'po-merge-approved'. It makes an accidental or automatic merge impossible and records every approval (actor and time) in the pull request timeline and in the check's log; the procedural rule is that the label is applied only after an explicit Product Owner merge instruction, or when the mission itself authorized the merge in advance.
residual_risks.authorization_workflow_editable_by_a_bra: The authorization workflow runs on pull_request, so its YAML is taken from the pull request's merge ref; a branch that edited that YAML could change the check that judges it. The decision logic itself is read from the base branch, and a change to either file is a governance change that FULL CHECK's delivery-protocol validator asserts. pull_request_target would pin the YAML to master but attaches its check to the base commit rather than the pull request head, so it cannot serve as the required context.

full_check_gates._why: Not required status checks. Each runs only when dispatched for FULL CHECK THE WHOLE CODE (tools/full-check.py). tools/validate-delivery-protocol.py asserts that none of them can be triggered by a pull request, a push or a schedule, and that each can be dispatched.
